summary: Official information is now honest across the lower 48 (CONTRACT §14.5-14.9, both ends). Backend: a state registry (fire3d/sources/evacuations.py) with Cal OES moved behind one adapter (California answers keep every brief-2 key and value, checked key by key against the brief-2 code's answers) and a new Oregon OEM adapter; every other state, Washington and Florida included, answers state_not_available with the §14.14 sentence and no upstream request; border dedup, explicit outFields, the EV-R6 status fix, cameras outside California answer state_not_available. Web: 'not available in this state' everywhere without a feed, no California rectangle in any evacuation or NWS path (the point's state from /api/geo/lookup and the answer's states_checked decide), source-neutral wording from sources[] (Oregon levels shown with OEM's definitions and 'added to the Oregon state layer'), source-neutral agency records (CAL FIRE or NIFC WFIGS, labelled from recordIssuerLabel, disagreement blocks, complex members, synthetic/not-checked states), the national NWS wording ('Official now · lower 48 states' only with all 49 codes, each alert in its own zone), local officials' alerts relayed by NWS and archived by FEMA with the OpenFEMA notice and a link on every message, the us-official dev preset, and the time migration of every owned file (check-time-api 0 and 0). Milestones M1-M6 and both cut-line items are done. The orchestrator's relayed issues (Horse Gulch data status in PDT, repeated not-available text without a full stop, WFIGS fires showing a CAL FIRE card, OpenFEMA notice, 'OFFICIAL NOW California') are fixed and checked on Horse Gulch.

contract_deviations: §14.8.2: sources[] entries also carry 'aggregator' ('Cal OES' / 'Oregon OEM'), additive, so the web never derives the short name from 'publisher'.
§14.8.1: EvacAdapter has three derived properties (upstream_name, layer_what, none_caveat); no extra dataclass fields.
§14.14: several uncovered states read 'Official evacuation zones are not available in these states (Nevada, Utah). Follow local officials.' (the contract has only the singular sentence).
§14.8.3: the state check runs before the past-date check, so a past time in a state without a feed answers state_not_available (California past answers unchanged).

§14.7 card line: the link is in OfficialLine.url with a new optional urlLabel ("issuer's link", 'source record (NWS)', 'source record (FEMA archive)'); us-web's OfficialSection still renders 'Read it'.
§14.5: OfficialInfo.calfire keeps its field name but holds the source-neutral RecordStatus (CAL FIRE or NIFC WFIGS).
§14.7: the quoted text prefers the WEA text, then the headline, then the description, cut at 220 characters with '…' (full texts behind 'More').

§14.6 wave-1 screenshot expectations (overview naming California; Reno 'NWS not checked') no longer apply: us-pipeline's national endpoint is live, so the overview says 'lower 48 states' and Reno is checked; the California-only behaviour is covered by unit tests against a CA-only answer.
§14.9.3 checker: four tz-ok opt-outs (listed under verification); review round 1 adds 8 more, all recorded zones of the new LOCAL_ARCHIVE_EATON fixture (12 in all).

§14.8.7: the dev preset's national NWS answer has Mountain-time alerts only (the only recorded national answer); the second zone is shown through local alerts (Pacific and Mountain), not by merging another day's alert (review R3).

§14.7: local-alert lines carry a location phrase ('area covers the fire's reported location' / 'area N mi from the fire's reported location · may be about another fire' / 'matched by county …'), the web orders them by relevance (in effect, covering, nearest, newest), and the location card keeps only the messages whose area reaches its point (localAlertsAtPoint, 1 km); additive LocalAlertItem fields nearestKm, where, polygon, sameCodes, LocalAlertsOfficial.elsewhere, OfficialPlace.countyFips (review R1).
§14.8.6: a state_not_available cameras answer has sources [] (review R5); §14.8.3: in an answer covering several states, Cal OES's none caveat names its source (review R6).

issues.R1: fixed. Verified: on Eaton at the replay time the answer lists LA City's Sunset Fire / Runyon Canyon messages (29.5, 26.2, 26.5 km) first and the rows had no location context. Now LocalAlertItem keeps nearestKm and adds where {from fire|point, covers, km}, polygon and sameCodes; localAlertOrder sorts in effect first, then the area covering the location, then the nearest, then the newest (Eaton: LACo OEM's orders at 1.0-2.7 km first). localAlertPlace adds the location phrase to every line in Official now, the feed (detail) and the card (sub and subCompact): 'area covers the fire's reported location' / 'area 1.7 mi from the fire's reported location · may be about another fire' / 'matched by county, not by an exact area · may be about another fire', in the viewer's units. Official now adds '34 messages for this fire's area; in effect first, then the nearest to its reported location:' and LOCAL_PLACE_NOTE under More. The location card measures from its point (localAlertsAtPoint): only messages whose area covers the point or lies within 1 km (about the live card's ?bbox= box; county matches in the point's county via geo lookup), the rest counted ('27 of the fire's local alerts are for other places in its area (see Updates).'), 'area covers this point' first. Wording differs from the reviewer's proposal on purpose: 'the message does not say which fire it is about' is false for messages that name their fire (Kern 'Cyrus Fire updated to an Evacuation Order'), and Fire-3d never reads the text, so lines say 'may be about another fire' and the note says Fire-3d ties a message to the fire only by where its area lies. Distances say 'from the fire's reported location' because that is what nearest_km measures (not the fire's edge). Tests: localAlerts.test.ts (4 new cases on LOCAL_ARCHIVE_EATON, 8 of the 33 messages of Fire-3d's own Eaton answer recorded 2026-10-23: nearest in-effect message first, ended last, a covering area first, the phrase on every feed row and card line in mi and km, the point filter and elsewhere count, the county match at a point), location/official.test.ts (every local line's sub and subCompact has the phrase).
